summary.title: Introduction to architecting systems for scale
summary.one_liner: Learn the core building blocks of scalable web systems: load balancing, caching, cache invalidation, off-line processing with message queues, map-reduce, and platform layers.
keywords: how to scale a web application
takeaways: Scale horizontally and build redundancy by spreading load across many machines, usually with load balancing at several layers.
Software load balancers like HAProxy are a good default; move to smart clients or hardware load balancers only when there is a clear need.
Introduce a consistent caching strategy early (application and database caching, in-memory stores, CDNs), and plan carefully for cache invalidation.
Move slow or periodic work off the request path using message queues and consumer pools, and consider a platform layer to scale both systems and teams.
summary.summary: The author, drawing on experience at Yahoo! and Digg, walks through the main building blocks of scalable systems. Topics include horizontal scaling and redundancy via load balancing (smart clients, hardware, and software load balancers), caching at the application, database, and CDN levels, and the difficulties of cache invalidation. It then covers off-line processing with message queues, periodic task scheduling, map-reduce, and the case for a separate platform layer. The post is an opinionated essay with code examples and diagrams rather than a step-by-step tutorial.
